subject: Results comparison of Stan and Winbugs

messages.author: 7fffd6a458b15b54
messages.subject: Results comparison of Stan and Winbugs
parts:
Hi Bob,
I am trying to compare Stan and Winbugs running a multilevel Item Response Model with both testlet effects and teacher effects. It took Winbugs more than 10 hours to converge, and it seems that the parameters are reasonably recovered (the true testlet variance value is 0.25, and the person variance is 1). It took Stan less than 2 hours to converge, which is considerably faster than Winbugs, but it seems that the estimates are really off. This really does not make sense to me, since I literally translates the Winbugs codes to Stan and all the priors are the same. Would it be possible for you to offer some advice? I  attached the results, the Winbugs codes, and my Stan codes. A million thanks!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Results comparison of Stan and Winbugs
parts:
Just taking a quick look, it doesn't look like the models are specified in the same way.

As an example, the prior for testlet is
WinBUGS:

testlet1[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau1)
testlet2[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau2)
testlet3[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau3)
testlet4[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau4)
testlet5[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau5)
testlet6[j] ~ dnorm(0,tau6)

where tau1 to tau6 are parameters (as far as I can tell)

Stan:

testlet1 ~ normal(0,1);
testlet2 ~ normal(0,1);
testlet3 ~ normal(0,1);
testlet4 ~ normal(0,1);
testlet5 ~ normal(0,1);
testlet6 ~ normal(0,1);


It's great that you're trying to do the comparisons. Just a couple notes:
- it's easy, but tedious translating models from BUGS to Stan. A bunch of the developers have gone through the painstaking exercise of specifying models in the Stan language, so it can be done. You have to be very, very careful and understand the differences in parameterizations.
- make sure the data is being read in correctly. If I'm remembering correctly, I think BUGS reads in matrices in row-major order. Stan reads matrices in column-major order.

My suggestion is to try specifying the Stan model again because it isn't a translation of the WinBUGS model. It's a different model and it might be operating on "different" data. For more guidance, look through the BUGS models we've already translated.


Daniel
